# 13. MOS calls

The MOS entry points have the BBC's low bytes in page &C7 (`OSWRCH` is
&C7EE where a BBC has &FFEE); the RAM vectors are at &0200 as on the
BBC. Programs call them with `CALL` or `USR` (A%, X%, Y% are passed in
the registers).

#### `MOS`

The MOS (machine operating system) entry points, at BBC Micro low bytes in page &C7:

```
OSFIND &C7CE   OSGBPB &C7D1
OSBPUT &C7D4   OSBGET &C7D7
OSARGS &C7DA   OSFILE &C7DD
OSRDCH &C7E0   OSASCI &C7E3
OSNEWL &C7E7   OSWRCH &C7EE
OSWORD &C7F1   OSBYTE &C7F4
OSCLI  &C7F7
```

The RAM vectors are at &0200-&021F as on a BBC Micro (BRKV &0202, WRCHV &020E, ...). See OSBYTE, OSWORD and VDUCODES.

#### `OSBYTE`

OSBYTE calls (*FX a,x,y) available:

```
&00   OS version (X=1)
&0F   flush keyboard buffer
&15   flush keyboard buffer
&72   shadow for next MODE
&75   VDU status (4: shadow)
&7C   clear ESCAPE
&7D   set ESCAPE
&7E   acknowledge ESCAPE
&7F   EOF# of channel X
&81   INKEY
&82   high address (&FFFF)
&83   OSHWM / PAGE (&1D00)
&84   HIMEM of the mode
&85   HIMEM for a mode
&86   POS (X) and VPOS (Y)
&87   character at cursor
&CA   keyboard status (CAPS LOCK)
&DA   VDU queue length
&E5   ESCAPE key off (X<>0)
```

Other calls are ignored.

#### `OSWORD`

OSWORD calls available: 0 reads a line (the line editor, *EDIT), 1 reads TIME, 2 sets TIME (5 bytes, centiseconds), 9 reads a pixel (POINT), 10 reads a character definition (block +0 = character; +1 to +8 = rows), 14 reads the Ultimate's clock, &42 copies between memory and the REU (block +0: &80 to the REU, 0 from it; +1/+2 address; +5/+6 length; +7 the REU's 64K bank (4-255); +8/+9 address in the bank; as the Master's sideways RAM transfer), &70 reads a value of the JSON reply *JSON GET keeps (see *JSON). Others are ignored.

OSWORD 14 as on a BBC Master: put 0 in the first byte of a 25-byte block for the text "Wed,07 Oct 2026.08:42:55" and a CR, or 1 for 7 BCD bytes: year (2 digits), month, day, day of week (1 = Sunday), hour, minute, second.

```
DIM B% 25:?B%=0:A%=14
X%=B% MOD 256:Y%=B% DIV 256
CALL &C7F1:PRINT $B%
```

#### `*FX`

```
*FX a[,x[,y]]
```

Calls OSBYTE a with X=x and Y=y. See OSBYTE.

```
*FX 15     flush the keyboard buffer
```
